page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-96 is a memory-oriented virtual machine configuration powered by AMD EPYC 7B13 processors built on the x86_64 architecture. The system provisions 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical execution cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is dense, offering 768.0 GB of system RAM at a ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware vector acceleration includes standard AVX, alongside hardware cryptographic instruction support including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, though AVX-512 extensions are absent. The configuration includes no onboard local storage or dedicated hardware GPUs, relying completely on external network-attached persistent disks for I/O operations.

Benchmark measurements reflect robust multi-threaded compute and in-memory processing capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier performance in stress-ng multi-core testing (129,681.93) and PassMark CPU encryption (102,726.49), supported by strong Geekbench multi-core (16,517.0) and PassMark overall CPU scores (79,745.05). In-memory caching operations are strong, demonstrating 81.23 million Redis SET operations per second and cached memory bandwidth of 5,754.6 GB/sec. Uncached large-block memory read throughput (143.05 GB/sec) and single-core compute performance settle in the mid-range tier, indicating that scaling across parallel threads is required to capture the full compute potential of the host.

Resource allocation delivers solid qualitative efficiency for enterprise memory scales, consolidating large footprints without requiring specialized ultra-high-memory bare-metal tiers. The lack of integrated local NVMe storage requires architectural reliance on network storage volumes, which limits native disk I/O performance. Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-96 fits large in-memory databases such as Redis or Memcached, high-capacity relational database management systems, data processing pipelines, static web distribution clusters, and parallel compilation environments.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-96 is an x86_64 virtual instance built on AMD EPYC 7B13 processors, providing 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores alongside 768.0 GB of system memory. It maintains an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio suited for large-footprint tasks. The server features no local storage or hardware accelerators, depending on remote block storage for persistence. In benchmark tests, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-core computing and cryptographic throughput, complemented by strong results in PassMark database execution and Redis operations exceeding 81 million operations per second. While single-thread speeds and uncached memory transfers rank near platform averages, its massive RAM capacity and parallel thread density make it suitable for large in-memory key-value stores, enterprise database workloads, complex ETL processing, and high-throughput static web distribution.
